question: Which crypto payment cards ("U cards") are still being issued on 2026-11-19, who issues each one, and what do their own official pages say they cost?
method: Official pages only (operator and issuer domains, US government sources for the FinCEN order, Taiwan SFB and the Taiwan VASP association for the regulatory column). Read without logging in, by plain HTTP download or in a browser where a site blocks plain requests. Third-party review, news and SEO sites were used only to find official URLs, never as the source of a figure. Card records were collected in three batches (cards_a, cards_b, cards_c below) and keep, for every data point, the source URL, a short verbatim quote and the page's own date. Bybit Card figures are taken from research/bybit_card_2026-11-19.json and were not re-fetched.

derived.assumptions: Example 1: one purchase worth 100 USD in a currency other than USD (and other than the card currency), paid from USDT, lowest or free tier, no promotions, the only purchase of the month. Cost = top-up fee + crypto conversion fee + foreign-currency fee, added (not compounded). Cashback counted at the base rate on the purchase amount. Card-network exchange rates, the platform's own USDT/USD rate and one-off card issuance fees are not included. Example 2: one ATM withdrawal abroad of local currency worth 500 USD (and 100 USD), first withdrawal of the month, physical card, paid from USDT. Fees charged by the ATM operator and dynamic currency conversion are not included. A card enters these tables only if its official pages give a top-up fee, a conversion fee and a foreign-currency fee (as a number or as explicitly none); cards with a missing component are listed separately as lower bounds.

method_notes: All facts read on 2026-11-19 from operator/issuer-published pages on the operator's own domains. Nothing was filled from memory or third-party sites.

Reading method per site: binance.com and gate.com via the Browser pane (rendered page text); okx.com, bitget.com, web3.bitget.com, bingx.com, kucoin.com announcements via raw HTML download + text extraction (verbatim grep); gate.com English wording via WebFetch (summariser) cross-checked against the zh-TW page text rendered in the browser.

The researcher's IP is geolocated in APAC (gate.com auto-served zh-TW; Binance landing API returned the APAC programme). Binance and Gate landing pages are geo-dependent, so another region may see different numbers.
Quotes that are table rows are reproduced as cell text separated by ' | '. Gate fee tables are quoted in Traditional Chinese exactly as rendered (gate.com forced zh-TW in the browser).
okx.com/card in the browser hit a CAPTCHA (not bypassed); its collapsed FAQ answers are not in the server-rendered HTML, so only the visible hero text of that page was read.
web3.bitget.com help-centre articles carry no per-article date; only section-level update timestamps exist in the page data (APAC section: 2026-01-07).
